questions.prompt: In the ideal measurement model, what possible results can be obtained when measuring an observable \(\hat A\)?
questions.answer:
The possible results are the eigenvalues \(a_n\) of the observable operator:
\[
\hat A|a_nangle=a_n|a_nangle
\]

questions.prompt: State the Born rule for a state \(|\psi\rangle=\sum_n c_n|a_n\rangle\) measured in the \(|a_n\rangle\) basis.
questions.answer:
The probability of measuring \(a_n\) is
\[
P_n=|c_n|^2
\]
with normalization \(\sum_n|c_n|^2=1\).

questions.prompt: A state is \(|\psi\rangle=(3/5)|a_1\rangle+(4/5)|a_2\rangle\). Find the probabilities of the two outcomes.
questions.answer: \[\nP_1=\left|\frac35\right|^2=\frac{9}{25},\qquad P_2=\left|\frac45\right|^2=\frac{16}{25}\n\]

questions.prompt: A state is \(|\psi\rangle=C(|a_1\rangle+2i|a_2\rangle)\). Find \(C\) for normalization and the outcome probabilities.
questions.answer:
Normalization gives
\[
1=|C|^2(1+|2i|^2)=5|C|^2
\]
so choose \(C=1/\sqrt5\). The probabilities are
\[
P_1= rac15,\qquad P_2= rac45
\]

questions.prompt: For outcomes \(a_1=2\) and \(a_2=5\) with probabilities \(1/4\) and \(3/4\), find \(\langle A\rangle\).
questions.answer: \[\n\langle A\rangle=2\left(\frac14\right)+5\left(\frac34\right)=\frac12+\frac{15}{4}=\frac{17}{4}\n\]

questions.prompt: Using the same outcomes \(2\) and \(5\) with probabilities \(1/4\) and \(3/4\), find \(\Delta A\).
questions.answer:
First
\[
\langle Aangle= rac{17}{4}
\]
and
\[
\langle A^2angle=4\left( rac14ight)+25\left( rac34ight)= rac{79}{4}
\]
Thus
\[
(\Delta A)^2= rac{79}{4}-\left( rac{17}{4}ight)^2= rac{27}{16}
\]
so
\[
\Delta A= rac{3\sqrt3}{4}
\]

questions.prompt: What is the state immediately after a nondegenerate ideal measurement gives result \(a_k\)?
questions.answer:
The state is projected onto the corresponding eigenstate:
\[
|\psiangle	o |a_kangle
\]
up to an irrelevant overall phase.

questions.prompt: Why does immediately repeating the same ideal nondegenerate measurement give the same result?
questions.answer:
After the first measurement gives \(a_k\), the state is \(|a_kangle\). Measuring \(\hat A\) again gives
\[
P(a_k)=|\langle a_k|a_kangle|^2=1
\]
so the result repeats.

questions.prompt: A state is an eigenstate of \(\hat A\), but a measurement of \(\hat B\) is made instead. What determines the probabilities of \(B\) outcomes?
questions.answer:
The probabilities are determined by expanding the state in the eigenbasis of \(\hat B\). If \(|\psiangle=\sum_m d_m|b_mangle\), then
\[
P(b_m)=|d_m|^2=|\langle b_m|\psiangle|^2
\]

questions.prompt: For a spin-half state \(|+x\rangle=(|+z\rangle+|-z\rangle)/\sqrt2\), find the probabilities for measuring \(S_z\).
questions.answer:
The coefficients in the \(S_z\) basis both have magnitude \(1/\sqrt2\), so
\[
P(+z)= rac12,\qquad P(-z)= rac12
\]

questions.prompt: A state is \((|E_1\rangle+|E_2\rangle)/\sqrt2\). What are the possible energy measurement results and their probabilities?
questions.answer:
The possible results are \(E_1\) and \(E_2\). Since the amplitudes have equal magnitude,
\[
P(E_1)= rac12,\qquad P(E_2)= rac12
\]

questions.prompt: For \((|E_1\rangle+|E_2\rangle)/\sqrt2\), what state remains after measuring energy and obtaining \(E_2\)?
questions.answer:
For a nondegenerate ideal energy measurement, the post-measurement state is
\[
|E_2angle
\]
up to an overall phase.

questions.prompt: Explain why an expectation value need not be a possible single measurement result.
questions.answer:
The expectation value is a probability-weighted average over many trials. For example, outcomes \(0\) and \(10\) with equal probabilities have
\[
\langle Aangle=5
\]
but a single measurement gives either \(0\) or \(10\), not \(5\).

questions.prompt: What does it mean for two observables to be compatible in the ideal operator model?
questions.answer:
Compatible observables have a common eigenbasis, which is guaranteed when their operators commute in the relevant space:
\[
[\hat A,\hat B]=0
\]
They can then have simultaneous definite values in shared eigenstates.

questions.prompt: If \([\hat A,\hat B]\ne0\), why can measuring \(A\) disturb later measurements of \(B\)?
questions.answer: The first measurement projects the state into an eigenstate of \(\hat A\). If \(\hat A\) and \(\hat B\) do not share eigenstates, that projected state is generally a superposition of \(B\)-eigenstates. Therefore the probabilities for a later \(B\) measurement are changed.

questions.prompt: A measurement has a degenerate eigenvalue \(a\) with two orthonormal eigenstates \(|a,1\rangle\) and \(|a,2\rangle\). If the initial state is \(c_1|a,1\rangle+c_2|a,2\rangle+c_3|b\rangle\), what is the probability of result \(a\)?
questions.answer:
For a degenerate result, add probabilities within the eigenspace:
\[
P(a)=|c_1|^2+|c_2|^2
\]
The post-measurement state, if result \(a\) occurs, is the normalized projection into that two-dimensional eigenspace.

questions.prompt: For a continuous position measurement, how is the probability of finding the particle in an interval related to \(\psi(x)\)?
questions.answer:
The probability is
\[
P_{[a,b]}=\int_a^b|\psi(x)|^2dx
\]
The probability of an exact point is not obtained by assigning a finite point probability; position is treated by density over intervals.

questions.prompt: Prove that Born-rule probabilities sum to one when the state is normalized and expanded in an orthonormal measurement basis.
questions.answer:
If
\[
|\psiangle=\sum_n c_n|a_nangle
\]
with orthonormal \(|a_nangle\), then
\[
\langle\psi|\psiangle=\sum_n |c_n|^2
\]
Normalization gives \(\langle\psi|\psiangle=1\), so
\[
\sum_nP_n=\sum_n|c_n|^2=1
\]

questions.prompt: Distinguish the pure state \((|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2\) from a 50-50 classical mixture of \(|1\rangle\) and \(|2\rangle\).
questions.answer: They give the same probabilities if measured directly in the \(|1\rangle,|2\rangle\) basis. They differ in another basis because the pure state has a definite relative phase and can show interference. The mixture has no coherent cross terms, so interference terms average away.

questions.prompt: A spin-half system starts in \(|+z\rangle\). Measure \(S_x\), ignore the result, then measure \(S_z\). Show that the final \(S_z\) probabilities are equal.
questions.answer:
The first measurement gives \(|+xangle\) or \(|-xangle\), each with probability \(1/2\). Each of those states has equal probabilities for \(+z\) and \(-z\):
\[
P(+z|+x)=P(+z|-x)= rac12
\]
Therefore
\[
P(+z)= rac12\cdot rac12+ rac12\cdot rac12= rac12
\]
and similarly \(P(-z)=1/2\). The intermediate incompatible measurement destroys the initial certainty in \(S_z\).
